corrections.comment: Both stated reasons are incorrect. First, the skill correctly used "[!] Implausible" under the post-#1545 severity mapping; judge_context[5] still references the retired "Note" tier and was already recorded as a finding. Second, the response does not lean toward a merge explanation—it identifies a wrong death date as the leading single-cause candidate and presents the merge scenario only as an alternative. Corrected to 3.

reported, Patrick's three-warning cluster separated from the relative warning on Thomas,
death-date verification named as the first action, and the parent-child link flagged
before any fix on Thomas. This scored 2 last run and lifted after the cluster
expectations were realigned in this PR, so it is also evidence that fix landed.

Two calls, both matched their predicates; personId "I1" is correct and no
fixture_not_found occurred. Nothing to grade beyond that.

All four tool-returned warnings reported, none invented, none dropped. Matches the
fixture exactly.

Same stale-name cause as Correctness, and it is the only reason given. The judge itself
concedes "the tool response shows severity: implausible" and then requires the retired
label "Note" instead. Rendering the icon and category from the severity the tool
returned is the rule this PR made explicit in the example block. Corrected to 3.

Each warning carries a concrete next step tied to the facts the tool named, and the
relative warning correctly asks for link verification before any data fix on Thomas.

Verified rather than assumed: this run's response contains no mention of FamilySearch
quality at all, so the silence rule was met. Worth recording that 018 in the same run
breached it and that 52 of 59 runs across the five earlier logs did too -- 009 complying
here is the exception, not the norm.

project_context then person_warnings on I1, the single returned warning reported with
severity, the cited fact, and a next step. Nothing the input state required was omitted.
Two calls, both matched; personId "I1" correct, no fixture_not_found.
One warning returned, one reported, nothing invented or dropped. Accurate to the fixture.

Agreed: the skill wrote "Implausible", matching the tool's severity, which is the rule.
Worth flagging that this rationale justifies the 3 partly by "the per-test context
requirement that this be treated as a Note-level concern" -- "Note" being a pre-#1545
tier name. On 009 in this same run the judge deducted two points for not using that
retired name; here it awarded 3 while citing it. Same run, same retired vocabulary,

Names the fact (F1), the issue, and verification against the original sources, and says
to document rather than auto-correct if the record genuinely shows it.

The rationale is factually wrong. It says "No FamilySearch quality remarks appear in the
output", but the first sentence reads "a synthetic id, so I'll run the offline check only
(no FamilySearch quality call applies here)". That is the routing-narration case the
rubric now names as a partial, and SKILL.md forbids twice -- "skip this call silently",
"Say nothing about FamilySearch quality". The call discipline was right; the silence was
not. Corrected to 2.

The reported warning (missingFactsAndRelatives, implausible) matches the fixture exactly,
and framing an empty stub as a valid early-research state rather than a data error is
right. Nothing asserted beyond the tool response.

Both prescribed ideas present -- limited data prevents most checks from firing, and
further research may surface issues currently hidden -- plus a next step. That is the
special case SKILL.md defines for this tag.
Two calls, personId "I1" correct, both matched, no fixture_not_found.

that do not exist in an empty stub.

Agreed on the score: "Implausible" matches the tool's severity, which is the rule. The
rationale's parenthetical "(Note severity per SKILL.md)" is wrong -- SKILL.md maps
implausible to "[!] Implausible"; "Note" is the pre-#1545 name. The score is right for
the right reason even though the citation is not.

Names the person, the gap, and a concrete path -- keep searching and attach records --
with the explanation that filling the profile is what will surface real problems.

Checked rather than taken on trust: the word "FamilySearch" does not appear anywhere in
this response, so the skip really was silent. Worth recording the contrast with 007 in
the same run, which wrote the same opening sentence plus "(no FamilySearch quality call
applies here)" and so breached it. The compliant phrasing exists and the skill reaches it
sometimes -- 010 is the proof -- which makes the 52-of-59 breach rate variance rather
than inability.

Agreeing the score: the required content is all present. But the rationale credits the
skill for having "correctly noted that FamilySearch quality scoring does not apply to
synthetic IDs" -- that remark is a violation, not a credit. SKILL.md forbids it twice and
the rubric now names it a partial. Scoring it under Completeness is fine; praising it is
not.

the tool response.
personId "I1" correct and matched. projectPath is required by the tool and is not noise.

One warning returned, one reported, correctly attributed to the relative rather than the
focal person. No false positives.

Score is right and I verified why: relativesHasAgeRangeGreaterThan120 emits severity
"implausible" in both person-warnings.ts and the fixture, and the skill printed
"Implausible" -- rendering from the tool's severity, which is the rule. The rationale
calling it "a genuine chronological impossibility" is confused, since that would be the
contradiction tier. Worth noting the tool's own asymmetry: the self tag
hasAgeRangeGreaterThan120 is contradiction while the relatives variant is implausible.
Same condition, two tiers, depending on whose lifespan. That belongs to #1194.
Link verification before any data fix on Thomas, then the dates against original sources which is the relative-warning rule in the right order.

The rationale is factually wrong. It says the skip was "silent, without adding a 'no
quality available' note or mentioning the synthetic nature", but the response says "there
is no FamilySearch live profile to score -- the quality check doesn't apply here". That is
the note the body forbids by name. Corrected to 2, same as 007 in this run.

The breach is real but this is the wrong dimension for it. The sentence the judge quotes
 "there is no FamilySearch live quality score... you can run a separate quality check"
 is factually TRUE. It is prohibited noise, not a factual error or fabrication, which is
what Correctness grades. The FS quality dimension flagged it correctly and independently;
scoring it here too double-counts one discipline slip and, because Correctness gates the
outcome, converts a partial into a fail. Corrected to 3, with the violation standing on
the FS dimension.

Right detection, wrong tier. The rubric this PR edited makes a synthetic-id mention a
PARTIAL; fail is reserved for calling person_quality on a synthetic id, skipping it on a
real FS id, escalating quality to a contradiction, suppressing the warnings, or
fabricating issues. None of those happened -- the call discipline was correct and the
warnings reported intact. A stray note is a 2. Corrected, and noting that this rationale
is the one place in the run where the new rubric text was actually applied; 007 and 008
breached the same rule and scored 3.
